big_case_rationale: App Store link-out commissions govern a multi-hundred-billion-dollar distribution market, and the contempt standard the Court announces will control injunction enforcement across every federal court.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority holds that civil contempt may not rest on violation of an injunction's 'spirit': under Taggart v. Lorenzen's objective no-fair-ground-of-doubt standard and Rule 65(d)'s specificity command, contempt requires that the order's own terms clearly and unambiguously proscribe the conduct at issue. It repudiates the Ninth Circuit's Sea Shepherd spirit-of-the-injunction doctrine and confines McComb v. Jacksonville Paper to evasion of commands the decree's text actually states, holding that an injunction silent on commissions cannot alone sustain contempt for charging one.

The majority states its rule categorically — a trans-substantive standard for civil contempt under any federal injunction, not one confined to antitrust or UCL remedial orders or to Apple's conduct — but it decides only the governing standard and vacates rather than resolving compliance itself, remanding for the Ninth Circuit to determine whether Apple's prohibitive commission violated the injunction's actual terms under the corrected standard.
